chapter: Opening and early New Orleans customs
title: Catholic musicians in early New Orleans bands; pianist Camilla Todd
summary: Charles says the early New Orleans players were all Catholic; he names pianist Camilla Todd, who came when piano replaced guitar.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Oh, Mr. Charles, I'm very much interested in knowing. How many of the men with whom you associated in the early days of jazz and New Orleans were Protestant and Catholic? I think this is important. Could you tell us?
Well, we only had, not during when I first went to New Orleans, we didn't have no Protestant at all. It was all Catholics.
And I believe you said that there was one fine pianist.
Because I could name you every one of them. You see, they were all Catholics.
You see, I'm on the board there.
Yes. And who was this fine pianist you told us about that later on that played?
Camilla Todd. Camilla Todd. Camilla Todd.
T-O-D-D. And you say she taught at one of the universities in New Orleans. That's right. Well, when did the Protestants begin to come into this scene?
Well, she came along with us on a later run when we started using piano. See, at first we didn't use piano. You see, we used to use the guitar. Yes. But afterward we put the piano in there.
